requirements.title: Intrinsic type specifications have six syntactic alternatives
requirements.source: 7.4.1 R704; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 80, printed 66, lines 7-12.
requirements.definition: An intrinsic-type-spec admits integer-type-spec, REAL with an optional kind selector, DOUBLE PRECISION, COMPLEX with an optional kind selector, CHARACTER with an optional character selector, or LOGICAL with an optional kind selector. DOUBLE PRECISION is a real specification, not a sixth intrinsic type or a form with an extra kind selector. The integer alternative expands through R705; character selectors retain their distinct grammar.
requirements.oracle: Six independently executed declaration controls cover all alternatives and the four locally displayed selector omissions/presences. Use KIND of standard default or double-precision literals, never assumed byte-valued kind codes. Each initialized object has an explicit value assertion.
requirements.oracle_limitation: These are admission controls, not full numeric, character or logical effects. Malformed descendant syntax stays with R705/R706 or the canonical character grammar rather than gaining a second rejection ID at this union. No DOUBLE COMPLEX extension, derived type, BOZ or arbitrary invalid twin is added.
requirements.dependencies: 7.3.2.1/R703 and 8.2/R801 supply declaration contexts. 7.4.3.1/R705, 7.4.3.2 p4-p5 (PDF 82), 7.4.3.3 p2-p3 (PDF 83), 7.4.4.2/R721-R723 (PDF 84-85), and 7.4.5 (PDF 87) retain their specific defaults and selectors. 4.1.2 p2 and 4.2 p2(3), PDF 45-46, supply the numbered reporting basis.

requirements.title: INTEGER admits an optional kind selector
requirements.source: 7.4.1 R705, PDF 80, printed 66, line 13; canonical keyword restatement in 7.4.3.1 p3, line 34.
requirements.definition: An integer-type-spec uses INTEGER and may include one kind-selector. The selector is not a storage-size notation. Its internal syntax and value restrictions are R706 and C717; omission denotes the default integer method under 7.4.3.1 p4.
requirements.oracle: Declare one default integer and one integer explicitly selected with KIND(0). Pass both initialized values to an explicit default-integer dummy and check their distinct values.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is a finite syntax/type admission control. Default-kind and minimum-range effects have primary ownership S7.4.3.1-004. A guessed misspelling or malformed selector is not manufactured as another invalid case for this optional wrapper.
requirements.dependencies: R704/R706/C717; 7.4.3.1 p3-p4, PDF 80; 15.5.2.5 supplies the exact intrinsic dummy type/kind premises. Existing R702/R703 and 7.3 catalogues retain their cases and ownership.

requirements.title: A kind selector encloses a scalar integer constant expression
requirements.definition: A kind-selector is parenthesized and contains a scalar integer constant expression, optionally preceded by KIND=. The expression need not be a literal, a bare name, or itself default integer. The value still has to meet C717. The scalar, integer and constant expression restrictions propagate from their canonical definitions; the selected type parameter's own default-integer kind is a different question.

pending.expression-category-diagnostics: Needs canonical, independently reviewed scalar-rank, integer-type and constancy diagnostic/control cases in actual kind-selector use, under C401, C1009 and C1014. Existing foundation IF and PDT C701 cases are not this use graph. No duplicate canonical ownership or intrinsic-selector surrogate for the PDT author's C701 work is introduced. This is bounded authorable canonical evidence, not an impossibility.

requirements.oracle: An unconditional runtime control uses positional and keyword forms with default-integer arithmetic constant expressions and supported KIND inquiries. A separate expression-kind control stores KIND(0) in an integer parameter selected with SELECTED_INT_KIND(18), but only after the existing integer-division profile bounds that identifier to ten decimal digits. This conservative bound guarantees the initialization conversion is representable in the mandatory range-18 method without ordering arbitrary kind identifiers or assuming that method is wider than default. Two compile-only pairs respectively supply a missing expression and repair a misspelled KIND keyword by one substitution. The misspelling is also declared as a valid supported integer constant in both sources, preventing an undeclared-symbol fallback from masquerading as a keyword report.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The selected expression kind can equal the default kind; no distinct-kind premise is invented. A larger default kind identifier makes only the separately qualified expression-kind witness unavailable, not the unconditional positional/keyword controls or mandatory integer support. Grammar reports must match the exact declaration and a case-specific expression or delimiter cause. Shared kind-selector nouns, implementation-facility failures and unrelated magnitude reports cannot pass. The qualified message alternatives describe observed diagnostic routes, not standard-prescribed wording. Required reporting is not mandatory fatal rejection; diagnose is used. Repairs are positive compile controls, not range or parameter-kind effects.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.3/R403/C401 (PDF 45), 10.1.9.1/R1027/C1009 (PDF 183), 10.1.12/R1032/C1014 and the constant-expression definition (PDF 187-188), C717, and 16.9.118/16.9.181 (PDF 424, 454-455). 8.5.13 p1 and 10.2.1.3 p8/Table10.9 require the initialization conversion to be representable. 7.4.3.1 p2 supplies mandatory integer capacity independently of the identifier-size profile; missing support is a failure, not an optional property.

requirements.title: A kind-selector value is nonnegative and supported for its type
requirements.definition: The scalar integer constant expression in a kind-selector has a nonnegative value and identifies a representation method available for the intrinsic type being specified. Numeric kind identifiers are processor- and type-specific. A real kind is also available for complex components as specified by 7.4.3.3. This R706 constraint does not replace the distinct character-selector constraint.
requirements.oracle: Eight compile-only pairs cover integer, real, complex and logical independently. Four unprofiled negatives change a supported inquiry-selected value to -1. Four further negatives use nonnegative zero only after an independent ISO_FORTRAN_ENV kind-inventory profile establishes its absence for that type; complex uses the real inventory. Every repair replaces only the selector value with a supported KIND inquiry. The profiles never compile the invalid declaration.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A negative selector is one defective value, though it necessarily also fails support; the absent-zero cases separate support from sign. Zero is not universally unsupported. On a processor supporting zero these optional witnesses are unavailable, not passes or waivers of C717; the unprofiled supported/negative witnesses remain. Diagnostic predicates bind the exact declaration, actual type, selector value and support cause. A constant-expression complaint cannot corroborate these scalar integer constant expressions, even if it mentions kind parameters. Unsupported-kind value reports remain intended evidence, while unsupported selector syntax, unrelated implementation failures, crashes, resource failures and summaries cannot corroborate. The qualified alternatives are observed diagnostic routes, not standard-prescribed wording. No storage width or universal kind-code mapping is asserted.
requirements.dependencies: R704-R706; 7.4.3.3 p2, PDF 83; 16.10.2.15 INTEGER_KINDS (PDF 474), 16.10.2.20 LOGICAL_KINDS (PDF 475), 16.10.2.26 REAL_KINDS (PDF 476), and 16.9.118 (PDF 424). 4.2 p2(3)-(4), PDF 46, supplies detection/reporting capability, not a prescribed message, severity or fatal exit. Character C724 remains outside this work unit.

requirements.title: An intrinsic KIND parameter itself has default integer type and kind
requirements.definition: Each intrinsic type has a kind parameter named KIND. The parameter itself is a default-kind integer value. Its value may designate a nondefault method of its object; that does not change the type or kind of the parameter inquiry. A KIND intrinsic result alone is not evidence that the parameter named KIND is implemented.
requirements.oracle: Five independent programs inquire value%KIND, check KIND(value%KIND) against KIND(0), and pass the inquiry to an explicit default-integer dummy that checks its value against an independent KIND inquiry. Real and complex objects use the guaranteed double-precision real method; no optional kind code is presumed.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The explicit dummy tests integer type as well as kind, which assignment conversion or equality of numeric kind identifiers alone would not establish. These are finite parameter-kind effects, not proof of every representation or all inquiry contexts. The earlier S7.2-002 programs remain unchanged and retain their general parameter-name/type ownership; this refinement is separately credited only to 7.4.1. Unsupported parameter-inquiry implementations are failed or source-only observations, not passing controls.
requirements.dependencies: 7.2 p2-p3, PDF 76, supplies the general parameter concepts. 9.4.5/R916/C923, PDF 153, supplies the parameter-name inquiry on initialized nonpointer/nonallocatable objects. 16.9.118, PDF 424, supplies the comparison inquiry. 15.5.2.5 supplies the explicit dummy's intrinsic type/kind agreement.

accounting.rationale: PDF 80 lines 3-4: classification partition and each of its five type members are separated below.
Intrinsic types are classified as numeric or nonnumeric. This taxonomy does not define new operations or require an executable category test.
Integer is numeric; its value and literal obligations are retained in 7.4.3.1.
Real is numeric; this does not duplicate 7.4.3.2 or its approximation requirements.
Complex is numeric, not a promise that every numeric relational operator accepts it.
Character is nonnumeric; its concatenation and relational rules retain Clause 10 ownership.
Logical is nonnumeric. A processor representation as bits or integers does not change its Fortran category.
The scalar premise comes through R403/C401; a kind-selector diagnostic use graph remains explicitly pending, without moving C401 ownership.
R1032's int-expr reaches R1027/C1009 (PDF 183). It is not permission to use a real constant that converts to integer.
R1032/C1014 and 10.1.12 retain constancy ownership, distinct from PDT C701.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and verified integration corrections: doc/source_audits/batch_009.json. Intrinsic taxonomy, every grammar alternative, default-integer KIND parameter type and the separate sign/support conditions retain their source premises. The selected-expression-kind control now has a sufficient independent conversion bound, while positional/keyword controls remain unconditional. All declaration negatives require case-specific grammar or actual type/value support causes. One canonical expression-category evidence facet remains pending.
